MARKE.|117 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>and others did cut boughes from the trees, and stravved them in the vvay. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=9}}† And they that vvent before and they that folovved, cried saying, Hosanna, ''blessed is he that commeth in the name of our Lord''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 117, 26.''}} {{verse|chapter=11|verse=10}}† ''blessed is the kingdom of our father Dauid that commeth, Hosanna in the highest''. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=11}}† And he entred Hierusalem into the temple: and hauing vevved al things round about, vvhen novv the euening houre vvas come, he vvent forth into Bethania vvith the Tvvelue.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|Mvnday}}.}}And the next day vvhen they departed from Bethania, he vvas an hungred. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=13}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 21, 19.''}}* vvhen he had seen a farre of a figtree hauing leaues, he came if happily he could finde any thing on it. And vvhen he vvas come to it, he found nothing but leaues. for it vvas not the time for figges. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=14}}† And ansvvering he said to it, Novv no man eate fruite of the any more for euer. And his Disciples heard it. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=15}}† And they come to Hierusalem.

And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 21, 12. Lu. 19, 45.''}}* vvhen he vvas entred into the temple, he began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and the tables of the bankers, and the chaires of them that sold pigeons he ouerthrevv. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=16}}† and he suffred not that any man should carie a {{sup|‖}} vessel through the temple: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=17}}† and he taught, saying to them, Is it not vvritten, ''That my house shal be called the house of prayer to al nations? But you haue made it a {{sup|‖}} denne of theeues''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 56, 7. Ier. 7, 11.''}} {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18}}† VVhich vvhen the cheefe Priestes and the Scribes had heard, they sought hovv they might destroy him. for they vvere afraid of him, because the vvhole multitude vvas in admiration vpon his doctrine. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}}† And vvhen euening vvas come, he vvent forth out of the citie.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=b The Gospel for S. Gregorius Thaumaturgus Nouemb. 17. And in a Votiue Masse for any necessitie.}}And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 21, 20.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|Tvesday}}.}}vvhen they passed by in the morning, they savv the figtree vvithered from the rootes. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21}}† And Peter remēbring, said to him, Rabbi, behold the figtree that thou didst curse, is vvithered. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22}}† b And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering saith to them, Haue {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Faith of God is to beleeue that he is able, and that he wil doe it if it be expedient, and no impediment on our part.}}∷ faith of God. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=23}}† Amen I say to you, that vvhosoeuer shal say to this mountaine, Be taken vp and be cast into the sea, and shal not stagger in his hart, but beleeue that vvhatsoeuer he saith, shal be done: it shal be done vnto him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=24}}† Therfore I say to you, al things vvhatsoeuer you aske, praying, beleeue that you shal receiue, and they shal come vnto you.⊣ {{verse|chapter=11|verse=25}}† And vvhen you shal stand to pray, forgiue if you haue ought against any man: that also your father which is in heauen, may forgiue you your sinnes: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=26}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ God neuer forgiueth sinnes to him that pardoneth not his enemies frō his hart. Whereby it is euident that more is required then only faith.}}∷ If so be that<noinclude>{{rh||P iij|you}}</noinclude>
